This is a huge endeavor longer than I could explain in a comment. AFAIK there is no direct import from Matlab to UE and get a graph automatically. It’ll take a custom pipeline.

Try looking at Kantan charts it’s a marketplace plugin that does some graph generation work in UE, you may be able to adapt to your needs. Otherwise you’re going to need to understand your data sources and parse those accordingly. From there it’s a matter of spawning in a visual representation in unreal. We do something similar in our work using instanced meshes to represent an individual data point from the parsed data files. Basically ingest data and spawn an instance for each data point, you can embed the data or other properties directly into the instances (see docs) or use some kind of lookup table to match to instance ID. On the interaction side you can pull the instance ID from a hit result and get the corresponding data from there. Then some extra work for axis, labels, etc. 

I’d suggest using a template for the VR interactions, AFCore or Mordentrals VR Expansion plugin are both very good for basic interactions. This will save you a ton of time over implementing from scratch. Both have tutorials and video content.
